Overview / Features / Safety & Medical Support
Before release · During work · At return

Safety belongs in the assignment.

A hazard changes the plan only when the people assigning and carrying out the work can see it. ArcHorizon links the hazard picture, operational risk assessment, release checks, weather, and field reports to the teams and tasks they affect.

Follow the release workflow ↓
Operational rhythm

Review risk at the points that matter.

Safety information starts before a team leaves and remains part of the assignment while conditions change.

01 / BEFORE

Understand the exposure

Identify hazards, relevant weather, terrain, access, and the team’s readiness. Record controls and release conditions.

02 / DURING

Watch changing conditions

Receive field hazard reports and weather alerts. Pass meaningful changes to operations and affected teams.

03 / AFTER

Carry lessons forward

Keep the safety narrative with the task, team, and incident record for follow-up assignments and reporting.

Hazards with location

Put the condition where the work is.

A hazard can be drawn on the operational map and connected to an assignment. Its location and description give planning, operations, and field personnel a common reference.

Map itUse a point or area for the affected location.
Explain itDescribe the condition and who or what it affects.
Act on itAdjust the route, assignment, briefing, or resource choice.
Explore operational mapping →
Operational risk management

Assess the task, then document the controls.

The operational risk matrix gives staff a consistent way to review specific hazards. SPE adds exposure to the discussion of consequence and likelihood. Record the factors, controls, and review decision alongside the work being released.

  • Evaluate the task and operating conditions.
  • Choose controls the team can actually apply.
  • Reassess when the hazard or assignment changes.
SPE risk assessment

Look at severity, probability, and exposure.

The SPE model gives Safety a structured way to assess a specific hazard before and after controls are applied. It makes the basis for a release discussion visible to the team and supervisor.

S

Severity

What is the credible consequence if this hazard results in harm?

P

Probability

How likely is the harmful event under the conditions of this assignment?

E

Exposure

How often, for how long, or how many people encounter the hazard?

Initial assessmentDescribe the hazard and evaluate the three factors.
ControlsChoose changes to the route, method, equipment, timing, or staffing.
Residual reviewReassess the remaining risk and record who reviewed the decision.

The assessment supports judgment and the appropriate release decision; the score does not make that decision on its own.

Ground resource release

A deliberate check before dispatch.

The Ground Release Officer can see whether the operational pieces are in place before a ground team moves: the assignment, the resource, the paperwork, and the conditions that govern release.

01Assignment ready

Task, supervisor, location, and hazards are clear.

02Team accountable

Personnel, status, and tracking are established.

03Paperwork complete

Required documents and briefings are accounted for.

04Conditions reviewed

Weather and safety triggers have been checked.

Weather as a safety input

A forecast matters when it changes the work.

Current conditions, the three-day outlook, NWS alerts, and aviation weather can inform a briefing or trigger reassessment. The weather workspace keeps the source information available while Safety records the operational response.

See the Weather workspace →
The field changes the picture

Make it easy to report what was found.

The companion app lets a team flag a new hazard from its assignment. The report can update the map and reach Safety, Operations, and Command in time to affect other work.

Field report→Map context→Task review
Medical support

Keep aid resources in the operational picture.

Safety planning includes where medical help is available, how it can be requested, and what conditions affect responders. Resource requests and significant field updates flow through Logistics and the incident record.

That connection helps command staff see which support resources are available to assigned teams.

Logistics & requests →Communications →Incident documentation →
